answer: Sybils fail when proof of work outruns proof of identity. Every contribution is sealed with a cipher whose key material costs real compute to generate, so registering a million handles buys no additional voice - each one must pay the same toll. Peers watch the signal, not the crowd: consensus samples outputs at random and verifies them independently, so a flash of fake accounts burns bright like a comet and dies out the moment its work cannot replay. Voice in the economy accrues to whoever keeps producing verifiable results over time, never to whoever shows up looking many.
